### O34876 — Cell division protein FtsX
- Organism: Bacillus subtilis (strain 168)
- Reviewed: True
- Source: local_uniprot_swissprot_xml
- Homology: identity=59.9%, query coverage=99.0%, target coverage=99.3%, E-value=1.13e-112
- function: Part of the ABC transporter FtsEX involved in asymmetric cellular division facilitating the initiation of sporulation. May act as an importer, possibly at the top of a hierarchical cascade leading to the correct temporal initiation of sporulation. Acts upstream of the histidine kinases KinA, KinB and KinC, the RapA phosphatase and the Spo0A sporulation protein.
- localization: Cell membrane; Multi-pass membrane protein; Membrane raft; Unlike the E.coli ortholog, localization is not restricted to division septa, nor is it dependent on FtsZ. Present in detergent-resistant membrane (DRM) fractions that may be equivalent to eukaryotic membrane rafts; these rafts include proteins involved in signaling, molecule trafficking and protein secretion (PubMed:23651456).
- subunit: Interacts with FtsE (Probable). Interacts with FloT (PubMed:23651456).
- GO: GO:0045121 | C:membrane raft | evidence=ECO:0000269
- GO: GO:0005886 | C:plasma membrane | evidence=ECO:0000314

- GO: GO:0045881 | P:positive regulation of sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore | evidence=ECO:0000316

### Q04LE4 — Cell division protein FtsX
- Organism: Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 2 (strain D39 / NCTC 7466)
- Reviewed: True
- Source: local_uniprot_swissprot_xml
- Homology: identity=41.4%, query coverage=97.6%, target coverage=98.1%, E-value=3.02e-60
- function: Part of the ABC transporter FtsEX involved in asymmetric cellular division facilitating the initiation of sporulation (By similarity). Required in maintaining normal growth and cellular morphology (PubMed:30696736).
- localization: Cell membrane; Multi-pass membrane protein
- subunit: Homodimer (PubMed:27167971). Interacts with FtsE; forms a membrane-associated complex (PubMed:22006325). Interacts (via large extracellular loop) with PcsB (via N-terminal coiled-coil domain) (PubMed:22006325, PubMed:30696736). This interaction directs PcsB to equatorial and septal sites of dividing cells (PubMed:22006325).
- GO: GO:0005886 | C:plasma membrane | evidence=ECO:0000269
